610-       are:
611-
612-       gitdir
613-	   The data that follows the keyword gitdir: is used as a glob
614-	   pattern. If the location of the .git directory matches the pattern,
615-	   the include condition is met.
616-
617-	   The .git location may be auto-discovered, or come from $GIT_DIR
618-	   environment variable. If the repository is auto-discovered via a
619-	   .git file (e.g. from submodules, or a linked worktree), the .git
620-	   location would be the final location where the .git directory is,
621-	   not where the .git file is.
622-
623-	   The pattern can contain standard globbing wildcards and two
624-	   additional ones, **/ and /**, that can match multiple path
625-	   components. Please refer to gitignore(5) for details. For
626-	   convenience:
627-
628-	   •   If the pattern starts with ~/, ~ will be substituted with the
629-	       content of the environment variable HOME.
630-
631-	   •   If the pattern starts with ./, it is replaced with the
632-	       directory containing the current config file.
633-
634-	   •   If the pattern does not start with either ~/, ./ or /, **/ will
635-	       be automatically prepended. For example, the pattern foo/bar
636-	       becomes **/foo/bar and would match /any/path/to/foo/bar.
637-
638-	   •   If the pattern ends with /, ** will be automatically added. For
639-	       example, the pattern foo/ becomes foo/**. In other words, it
640-	       matches "foo" and everything inside, recursively.
641-
642-       gitdir/i
643-	   This is the same as gitdir except that matching is done
644-	   case-insensitively (e.g. on case-insensitive file systems)
645-
646-       onbranch
647-	   The data that follows the keyword onbranch: is taken to be a
648-	   pattern with standard globbing wildcards and two additional ones,
649-	   **/ and /**, that can match multiple path components. If we are in
650-	   a worktree where the name of the branch that is currently checked
651-	   out matches the pattern, the include condition is met.
652-
653-	   If the pattern ends with /, ** will be automatically added. For
654-	   example, the pattern foo/ becomes foo/**. In other words, it
655-	   matches all branches that begin with foo/. This is useful if your
656-	   branches are organized hierarchically and you would like to apply a
657-	   configuration to all the branches in that hierarchy.
658-
659-       hasconfig:remote.*.url:
660-	   The data that follows this keyword is taken to be a pattern with
--
662-	   that can match multiple components. The first time this keyword is
663-	   seen, the rest of the config files will be scanned for remote URLs
664-	   (without applying any values). If there exists at least one remote
665-	   URL that matches this pattern, the include condition is met.
666-
667-	   Files included by this option (directly or indirectly) are not
668-	   allowed to contain remote URLs.
669-
670:	   Note that unlike other includeIf conditions, resolving this
671-	   condition relies on information that is not yet known at the point
672-	   of reading the condition. A typical use case is this option being
673-	   present as a system-level or global-level config, and the remote
674-	   URL being in a local-level config; hence the need to scan ahead
675-	   when resolving this condition. In order to avoid the
676-	   chicken-and-egg problem in which potentially-included files can
677-	   affect whether such files are potentially included, Git breaks the
678-	   cycle by prohibiting these files from affecting the resolution of
679-	   these conditions (thus, prohibiting them from declaring remote
680-	   URLs).
681-
682-	   As for the naming of this keyword, it is for forwards compatibility
683-	   with a naming scheme that supports more variable-based include
684-	   conditions, but currently Git only supports the exact keyword
685-	   described above.
686-
687-       A few more notes on matching via gitdir and gitdir/i:
688-
689-       •   Symlinks in $GIT_DIR are not resolved before matching.
690-
691-       •   Both the symlink & realpath versions of paths will be matched
692-	   outside of $GIT_DIR. E.g. if ~/git is a symlink to
693-	   /mnt/storage/git, both gitdir:~/git and gitdir:/mnt/storage/git
694-	   will match.
695-
696-	   This was not the case in the initial release of this feature in
697-	   v2.13.0, which only matched the realpath version. Configuration
